{{Short description|Philosophical position}}
In [[philosophy]], '''ontological maximalism (or metaontological maximalism)''' is a ontological realist position that asserts, "whatever can exist does in some sense exist".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Szubka |first=Tadeusz |url=https://brill.com/display/book/edcoll/9789004312654/B9789004312654-s012.xml |title=Metaontological Maximalism and Minimalism: Fine versus Horwich |date=2016-01-01 |publisher=Brill |isbn=978-90-04-31265-4 |language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
[[Meta-ontology]] deals with question related to ontology, whether there are mind independent (objective) answers to "what exists". Ontological realism asserts that reality (at least a part of it) is independent of the human mind.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Niiniluoto |first=Ilkka |title=Critical Scientific Realism |date=2002-02-07 |chapter=Realism in Ontology |pages=21–41 |chapter-url=https://academic.oup.com/book/1368/chapter/140678078 |language=en |doi=10.1093/0199251614.003.0002|isbn=0-19-925161-4 }}</ref> In contrast to realists, ontological anti-realists deny that the world is mind-independent. Believing the epistemological and semantic problems to be insoluble, they conclude that realism must be false.<ref>{{Citation |last=Khlentzos |first=Drew |title=Challenges to Metaphysical Realism |date=2021 |url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/spr2021/entries/realism-sem-challenge/ |encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy |editor-last=Zalta |editor-first=Edward N. |access-date=2023-03-21 |edition=Spring 2021 |publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University}}</ref>

Maximalism is one of two main metaontological positions. In a maximalist framework, any entity whose existence is consistent with the nature of this world can be taken to exist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chalmers |first=David |title=Ontological Anti-Realism |url=https://consc.net/papers/ontology.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211031162457/https://consc.net/papers/ontology.pdf |archive-date=Oct 31, 2021}}</ref>
